To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and developed a collaborative proxy system for the purpose of content adaptation.
we have developed a content adaptation framework which can be used for delivering Internet content to heterogeneous devices.
we have developed a content adaptation framework, called Naproxl, that addresses the problems of scalability, extensibility and adaptability of a content adaptation framework.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, development and evaluation of a collaborative proxy based content adaptation system.
a new approach to content adaptation, where the adaptation is driven by the client device capabilities, and the adaptation is performed in a peer-topeer organization of edge proxies.
the design and implementation of a collaborative proxy system that can provide a scalable content adaptation solution to the problem of delivering content to a large number of heterogeneous devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have proposed a content adaptation system which is extendable, scalable and efficient in terms of processing time, network usage and the amount of data that is transferred over the network.
the Naproxl framework can be used to develop a collaborative proxy network that is capable of adapting Internet content to a wide variety of client devices.

we have proposed and developed an architecture for a peer-to-peer collaborative proxy system for transcoding and content adaptation, and have implemented a prototype to prove that such a system is feasible and effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and implemented a framework that can be used for content adaptation in a collaborative peer-to-peer network.
the system is capable of providing a seamless experience to the user in the sense that the user is not aware of any content adaptation happening at the edge of the network.
the system has been designed to work in a peer-to peer environment and the edge nodes in the system can work in a collaborative fashion to process the content adaptation tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Naproxl framework can be used to develop a content adaptation system without disturbing the existing Internet content servers.
the content adaptation framework can be deployed in a distributed peer-to-peer organization without the need for any central server.
the proposed system is a generic framework for transcoding and content adaptation.
